countyFips.what: Most populous county (or county equivalent) in each state; DC is the District itself.
countyFips.publisher: U.S. Census Bureau, Vintage 2024 county population estimates (CO-EST2024-ALLDATA), POPESTIMATE2024, SUMLEV 050.
countyFips.note: Connecticut is reported on the nine planning regions that replaced its counties in 2022; 09110 is the Capitol Planning Region.

monthlyRent.what: Two-bedroom Fair Market Rent for that county, in whole dollars per month.
monthlyRent.publisher: HUD Office of Policy Development and Research, FY2026 Fair Market Rents, county level, revised schedule (fmr_2).
monthlyRent.vintage: FY2026 (effective 2025-10-01), revised schedule, which supersedes the unrevised FY26_FMRs.xlsx.
monthlyRent.note: In the six New England states HUD publishes FMRs by town, not by county, and a county can span two or three FMR areas. Those counties take the population-weighted mean of their town rows using HUD's own pop2023 column, rounded to the dollar: MA 25017 ($2,351/$2,941 across 54 town rows -> 2825), ME 23005 ($1,833/$2,130 across 28 town rows -> 2082), NH 33011 ($1,698/$2,037/$2,127 across 31 town rows -> 2058). CT 09110, RI 44007, VT 50007 are single-valued across their town rows. Every other state's county is one row.
monthlyRent.access: huduser.gov answers a plain request with an empty HTTP 202 bot challenge; scripts/build-state-defaults.mjs fetches this file through a proxy.

monthlyChildcarePreschool.what: Price of center-based care for a preschooler (ages 3-5) in that same county, in whole 2026 dollars per month.
monthlyChildcarePreschool.publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Women's Bureau, National Database of Childcare Prices (NDCP), variable MCPreschool (median weekly full-time price).
monthlyChildcarePreschool.vintage: NDCP study years 2008-2018; each state's county contributes its own most recent year with a price. See childcareBasis for which year that is, state by state.
monthlyChildcarePreschool.arithmetic: weekly price x 52 / 12 = monthly, then x the BLS Employment Cost Index factor from that study year to CY2026 (see eci), rounded to the dollar.
monthlyChildcarePreschool.fallback: The county's own price where it has one. Where it does not, the median across the state's counties (each at its own most recent year); where the state has no center-based price in any year, the median of the 2018 cross-section (2,360 counties, $730/month). On the state-median rule: CT. The NDCP is built on the eight pre-2022 Connecticut counties, so the Capitol Planning Region has no row of its own; Hartford County (09003), which that region largely replaces, is $1,425 on the same arithmetic against the $1,416 the state median gives. On the national-median rule, because the NDCP publishes no center-based price for them in any year: IN, NM.
monthlyChildcarePreschool.note: DOL's derived 'Childcare Prices by Age of Children and Care Setting' table (Data-Table-2023.xlsx) was NOT used: for the states the NDCP leaves blank in 2018 it carries the weekly price in an annual column, giving Denver County a $36,101/year preschool price and a $693,417/year home-based price.

eci.method: BLS Employment Cost Index, wages and salaries, private industry workers (index, not seasonally adjusted). Calendar-year average of the four quarterly index values, NDCP study year -> CY2026; quarters not yet published are extrapolated from the same quarter of the prior year at the latest published 12-month rate (3.138%). https://api.bls.gov/publicAPI/v2/timeseries/data/ did not serve the series on this run (it caps unregistered callers at 25 requests a day), so the quarterly values fetched from it on 2026-09-15 and compiled into scripts/build-state-defaults.mjs were used instead. crossCheck is what tests them: it is computed here and compared against a factor another builder derived from a live fetch.
eci.crossCheck: CY2024 -> CY2026 on this same arithmetic is 1.067533, the factor core/data/reach.json applies to the reach ladders.

childcareBasis.note: Which rule produced each state's monthlyChildcarePreschool and the NDCP study year behind it. 'county' is the most populous county's own MCPreschool — the household the row describes. 'stateMedianCounty' and 'nationalMedian' are the fallbacks, in that order; see sources.monthlyChildcarePreschool.fallback.
